description: Table 4 is a single rendered data table (no panels, no axes, no scale bar) listing calculated elastic-wave and thermal parameters for nine Fe1-xMnxAl compositions. The header row reads: Species; ρ/(kg·m⁻³); v1/(m·s⁻¹); vs/(m·s⁻¹); vm/(m·s⁻¹); ΘD/K. Rows, in order from top to bottom: FeAl (5935.5; 7644.2; 4492.6; 4979.7; 652.5), Fe0.875Mn0.125Al (5870.8; 7430.0; 4229.0; 4700.8; 614.0), Fe0.75Mn0.25Al (5807.7; 7292.2; 4048.7; 4509.5; 587.0), Fe0.625Mn0.375Al (5745.3; 7187.5; 3918.1; 4370.2; 567.3), Fe0.5Mn0.5Al (5678.2; 7012.6; 3687.3; 4123.3; 533.3), Fe0.375Mn0.625Al (5622.2; 7198.1; 3913.3; 4365.7; 563.1), Fe0.25Mn0.75Al (5565.7; 7249.4; 4007.8; 4465.4; 574.2), Fe0.125Mn0.875Al (5483.8; 7217.1; 3950.9; 4405.3; 564.0) and MnAl (5448.8; 6905.1; 3519.6; 3943.8; 504.1). The table shows density and all three sound velocities decrease monotonically from FeAl to MnAl, whereas ΘD falls to a minimum at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al (533.3 K) then rises to 574.2 K at Fe0.25Mn0.75Al before dropping again to 504.1 K for MnAl. The caption states these are theoretical (DFT) values.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table with header row 'Species, ρ/(kg·m⁻³), v1/(m·s⁻¹), vs/(m·s⁻¹), vm/(m·s⁻¹), ΘD/K' and nine data rows for FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl, each with density, longitudinal, transverse, average sound velocity and Debye temperature values.

observations.observation: The table header columns are Species, ρ/(kg·m⁻³), v1/(m·s⁻¹), vs/(m·s⁻¹), vm/(m·s⁻¹) and ΘD/K.
Nine compositions are tabulated: FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl.
FeAl has the highest tabulated density (5935.5 kg·m⁻³) and MnAl the lowest (5448.8 kg·m⁻³).
FeAl has the largest Debye temperature in the table, ΘD = 652.5 K.
MnAl has the smallest Debye temperature in the table, ΘD = 504.1 K.
ΘD decreases monotonically from FeAl (652.5 K) through Fe0.875Mn0.125Al (614.0), Fe0.75Mn0.25Al (587.0), Fe0.625Mn0.375Al (567.3) to a minimum of 533.3 K at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al.
Beyond Fe0.5Mn0.5Al the Debye temperature rises again to 563.1 K (Fe0.375Mn0.625Al) and 574.2 K (Fe0.25Mn0.75Al), then falls to 564.0 K (Fe0.125Mn0.875Al) and 504.1 K (MnAl).
The longitudinal sound velocity v1 falls from 7644.2 m·s⁻¹ for FeAl to 6905.1 m·s⁻¹ for MnAl, with the minimum all-composition value at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al (7012.6 m·s⁻¹) among the Mn-containing alloys.
The transverse sound velocity vs falls from 4492.6 m·s⁻¹ (FeAl) to 3519.6 m·s⁻¹ (MnAl), again with a local minimum of 3687.3 m·s⁻¹ at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al.
Density decreases monotonically with increasing Mn content across the whole series from FeAl to MnAl.
The caption states the tabulated values are theoretical (q / calculated) densities, longitudinal (ν1), transverse (νs), average (νm) sound velocities and Debye temperature (ΘD).
The citing text states FeAl has the largest ΘD of 652.5 K and concludes it therefore has stronger covalent bonds than the other Fe1-xMnxAl alloys.

The citing text states Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the highest B/G ratio (2.28) and the lowest ΘD (533.3 K) among the Fe0.875Mn0.125Al-to-Fe0.125Mn0.875Al range, indicating the strongest metallic character and weakest covalent bonds.
The citing text describes a V-shaped ΘD trend (decreasing to Fe0.5Mn0.5Al then increasing to Fe0.25Mn0.75Al then decreasing to MnAl), which matches the tabulated values in the image.
The citing text notes the B/G ratio of 2.52 and lowest ΘD of 504.1 K for MnAl; the ΘD value is visible in the table but the B/G ratio is not tabulated in this figure.
